questions.question: What prefix is required when declaring a CSS custom property?
questions.explanation: CSS custom properties must always begin with a double hyphen (--variable-name).

questions.question: Which CSS function retrieves and applies the value of a custom property?
questions.explanation: The var() function references the value of a CSS custom property.

questions.question: Where are global CSS custom properties conventionally declared so they cascade across the entire document?
questions.hint: :root matches the <html> element with higher specificity.
questions.explanation: Declaring custom properties in :root makes them globally accessible throughout the entire document tree.

questions.question: What is the role of the second argument in var(--accent-color, #2563eb)?
options: It acts as a fallback value if --accent-color is not defined
It limits the color to dark mode
questions.explanation: The second parameter in var() is a fallback value used if the referenced custom property is invalid or not defined.

questions.question: Are CSS custom property names case-sensitive?
options: No, CSS variables are completely case-insensitive
Yes, --primaryColor and --primarycolor are two distinct variables
questions.explanation: Unlike standard CSS property names, CSS custom property names are strictly case-sensitive.
